sources.entry: Metrune - Local-first focus workspace that brings tasks, AI coding, GitHub activity, device events, badges, and reports into the MacBook notch. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Metrune
summary.one_liner: Metrune is a free, local-first macOS app that puts focus timers, tasks, Codex and GitHub activity, device events, badges, and periodic reports into the MacBook notch.
use_cases: Run timed focus sessions tied to a specific task
Track daily GitHub activity and AI coding sessions in one place
See power, headphone, and keyboard connection events beside the notch
Generate weekly or monthly progress reports to share
Keep a local archive of focus history and badges
summary.what_it_does: Metrune is a macOS workspace that lives in the notch area. It has a task-based Focus timer with running, paused, break, and expired states, plus a compact mode. It shows Codex session state, 30-day AI coding activity, and read-only quota, and it displays public GitHub activity. Progress is tracked with a local avatar, levels, titles, an annual heatmap, and Focus, GitHub, and AI Coding badges. Weekly and monthly reports can be customized and exported as static files. Tasks, focus history, and badges stay on the Mac by default with no cloud account.
notable: Notch-based UI that shows task timer, device events, and music beside the physical notch
Local-first: no account, no auto-uploaded diagnostics, GitHub credentials and AI prompts not stored
Yearly heatmap, levels, and badge wall for accumulated work
caveats: v0.1.0 Community Release requires Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later
Not Apple-notarized; first launch may need right-click > Open in Finder
Listed as Freeware on awesome-mac; English, Chinese, and Japanese languages supported
